_about: Inventory of EXISTING electrical / plumbing terminations in flat 569 (bare shell, предчистовая отделка), read off four site photos. Coordinates in metres in the brief's system: X -3.45 (west) .. +3.45 (east), Z -1.405 (north wall of kitchen-living) .. +1.405 (south), Y = 0 floor, ceiling assumed 2.70. Every x/y/z is an ESTIMATE from photo geometry; the stated +/- is my honest belief, not a tolerance.

sources.photo-kitchen-sinkwall.jpg: kitchen (east) end of kitchen-living, looking east. Fully calibrated (see calibration note) - best coordinates in the set.
sources.photo-living-window.jpg: west (living) end of kitchen-living, looking west at the window wall.
sources.photo-bathroom.jpg: bathroom from its doorway looking north; the two devices at the bottom corners are in the hall.
sources.photo-bedroom.png: bedroom looking west; low-resolution video screenshot - weakest geometry.
sources.plan-569.jpg: developer plan, confirms kitchen-living 6.90 x 2.81 (window 1.70 + pier 1.10 on the west wall), bedroom 4.58 x 2.70 (window 1.60 + pier 1.10), bathroom 2.19-2.33 x 1.53, door 0.70.

assumptions: Ceiling height H = 2.70 m as instructed. See the discrepancy note - the photos do not actually confirm 2.70 and are internally more consistent with ~3.2-3.5 m, or with the images having been re-encoded with a non-square pixel aspect. Heights below were therefore derived PROPORTIONALLY (fraction of the visible floor-to-ceiling run x 2.70) wherever a floor line and a ceiling line were both visible, because that method is immune to a vertical stretch. It independently returned exactly 0.30 m for the three living-room sockets and 0.78 m for the window sill, which is why I trust it.

photo-kitchen-sinkwall.jpg was calibrated properly: vanishing points gave f = 628 px, then a least-squares fit of camera pose to the plan (east wall x=+3.45, partition z=-0.805, step x=+2.15, neighbours' wall z=+1.405) converged at camera = (x=+0.23, y=1.47, z=-0.04) with 5.9 px RMS over 5 control points and a best-fit ceiling of 2.76 m. Kitchen coordinates come from back-projecting image points onto the known wall planes; they are the most reliable here (+/- ~0.10-0.15 m).

Floor screed appears to be poured in all four rooms (a level grey screed is visible), so y = 0 is taken as the visible slab/screed surface. If a further levelling layer is added, every y shrinks by that thickness.

Grey bands running from sockets down to the floor are chased surface conduit (штроба + гофра) carrying the cable up out of the floor screed. They are recorded as conduit-run items because they fix where the supply enters.

Standard device sizes used as rulers: single socket/switch plate 80 mm, double socket plate ~145 mm, panel radiator 500 mm high, sewer stubs 50 mm and 110 mm, door leaf opening 0.70 m, window sill 0.80 m.
Water stub colour code read from raw pixel RGB, not from the auto-contrasted crops: red cap = hot, blue cap = cold, neutral grey circle = open pipe end (sewer).
No gas pipework, no electrical consumer unit / meter board, and no telecom/TV outlet is visible anywhere in the four photos.
discrepancies: GEOMETRY: in all four photos the walls image ~20-35% TALLER relative to their width than a 2.70 m ceiling allows for the plan's wall lengths. In photo-living-window the west wall images 288-302 px wide by ~365 px tall; with the plan's 2.81 m width that forces H ~ 3.4-3.5 m, and with H = 2.70 it forces a room width of only ~2.3 m. The same ~1.3x excess appears in the bathroom photo and a ~1.2x excess in the kitchen photo. Either the ceilings are much higher than 2.70, or the images were resized anamorphically (they have had all EXIF stripped, and photo-bedroom.png is flagged 'Screenshot'). This is why heights are proportional rather than absolute-scaled. MEASURE THE CEILING ON SITE before using any y value for cabinetry.

photo-living-window is internally inconsistent in one more way: the south-wall floor line is about twice as steep as a 2.81 m wide room with a 1.4-1.6 m camera height can produce, while the west wall's two corners place the camera near the room centre line. That is why the living-room ALONG-WALL (x) positions carry +/- 0.35-0.45 m, much worse than their heights.

PLAN MATCH that does hold: in photo-living-window the window frame measures 1.61 m spanning z = -1.36 .. +0.25, i.e. hard against the north corner with ~0.05 reveals - exactly the plan's 1.70 opening from z = -1.405. The window/wall width ratio is 0.59 vs the plan's 0.605. So the horizontal geometry of the plan is confirmed; only the vertical scale is in doubt.

The bedroom window likewise sits hard against the bedroom's NORTH wall (frame z = -4.14 .. -2.69, ~1.45 m, leaving a ~1.17 m pier on the z=-1.525 side), which matches the plan's 1.60 + 1.10 split on that wall.

No ventilation duct is visible in the bathroom - the bathroom ceiling is cut off at the top of photo-bathroom.jpg. A bathroom вентканал must exist; it is simply undocumented. Only the kitchen vent (K1) is visible.
The kitchen has THREE water stubs (cold / hot / cold, K3-K5) plus two open pipe ends low down (K6, K7). A third valve suggests a dishwasher or washing-machine tap was provided at the kitchen sink.

Socket heights are bimodal and consistent with a normal rough-in: ~0.28-0.30 m for all general-purpose sockets (K13, L4, L5, L6, B1) and ~1.05-1.20 m for the kitchen worktop group (K2, K9) and the bathroom box (W9).
undocumented_walls: Kitchen-living, south wall z=+1.405: only the eastern ~2.0 m (photo 1) and two points near the west end (photo 2) are seen. The middle ~2.5 m of this 6.90 m wall is in neither photo.

Kitchen-living, north wall z=-1.405: only around x = -0.8 (photo 2) is seen. The portion east of about x = +0.5, including the 0.92 m passage opening at x = 1.23..2.15 and its reveals, is not photographed.
Kitchen-living, east wall x=+3.45: only z = -0.805 .. +1.405 is visible (photo 1). Nothing north of the partition is seen.

Partition at z=-0.805 (x 2.15..3.45), south face: visible in photo 1 but only as a 95 px wide dark grazing sliver - I cannot say whether it carries any device. Its north (hall) face is not photographed at all.
Step wall at x=+2.15: only the lower part of its west face is in frame; above about y = 0.8 it is cut off.
Kitchen-living ceiling: only patches near both ends. The middle is unseen.
Bedroom: east wall (x=+1.13) and its doorway, the whole north wall except one socket, the ceiling, and the ceiling light drop point are undocumented or cut off.

Bathroom: east wall x=+3.45 except the one box near the north corner; the west wall x=+1.23 (only a grazing sliver); the south wall z=-2.68 interior face; the whole ceiling including the ventilation duct.

Hall: everything except the two devices flanking the bathroom door on z=-2.68. The entrance pocket (x 3.45..3.95), the front-door wall, the hall ceiling, and any consumer unit / meter cabinet are entirely undocumented.
Whole flat: no distribution board (щиток) is visible in any photo - its location is unknown.

items.note: Round white plastic cap protruding from the wall at the very top, image (397,37), outer diameter 40 px = ~0.19 m, its top edge touching the wall/ceiling line. Casts a clear shadow down-right so it stands proud of the plaster. z +/-0.10, y +/-0.12 (the cap straddles the ceiling junction, so 2.55 is the centre of a cap spanning roughly 2.45-2.70).
items.probable_use: Kitchen extract duct (вентканал) - the connection point for a cooker hood.

items.note: Rectangular dark recess in a light surround at image (381-434, 351-399), i.e. about 0.24 x 0.22 m on the wall - far too big for one socket, about right for a block of two or three ganged boxes, or for a single pattress with no faceplate. I genuinely cannot tell a socket from a blank box here; the image is soft. Directly above the water stubs K3-K5 and at classic over-worktop height. z +/-0.08, y +/-0.10 (proportional method gives 1.15, full calibration gives 1.29).
items.probable_use: Over-worktop socket block / junction for the kitchen sink run - probably the feed point for appliances at the sink.

items.note: Left valve of a three-valve group on a white plaster pad, image (412,539). Raw pixel colour (36,40,52) = dark BLUE cap, so cold. A white riser pipe runs from it straight down to the floor. z +/-0.06, y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: Cold feed - kitchen sink mixer or a machine tap.

items.note: Middle valve of the group, image (447,537). Raw pixel colour (83,45,39) = RED cap, so hot. White riser to the floor. Spacing from K3 is 0.165 m, to K5 0.145 m. z +/-0.06, y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: Hot feed - kitchen sink mixer.

items.note: Right valve of the group, image (476,537). Raw pixel colour (19,21,29) = dark BLUE cap, so a second cold. z +/-0.06, y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: Second cold tap - dishwasher or washing machine at the kitchen end.

items.note: Dark circular opening about 0.05 m across at image (462,571), raw colour (61,65,65) i.e. neutral grey/black - a pipe mouth seen end-on, not a coloured valve. Sits below and between K4 and K5. z +/-0.07, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: 50 mm waste stub for the kitchen sink / appliance drain.

items.note: Grey protrusion low on the wall just right of the stub cluster, image (497,592), raw colour (134,129,122) = unpainted grey PVC. Shape unclear; could be a second waste spigot, a socket for a 110 mm branch, or just a mortar lump. Recorded because it is clearly man-made pipework. z +/-0.10, y +/-0.08.
items.probable_use: Waste connection or capped branch at the kitchen sink.

items.note: Two white plastic risers run vertically from the valve pad (y ~0.40) down into the floor screed, image columns 410-422 and 433-447 ending at the floor line y~628. Recorded as one run; this is where the kitchen water supply enters, i.e. from the floor, not from the wall.
items.probable_use: Water supply risers from the screed to K3/K4/K5.

items.note: Unambiguous white DOUBLE socket, two round recesses in one horizontal frame, image (1053-1115, 458-505). Already carries a faceplate, unlike everything else in the flat. Plate measures ~0.145 m which is what fixes the local scale. x +/-0.25 (near the frame edge, so lens distortion bites), y +/-0.15 (back-projection says 1.17, the conduit length says 1.05-1.30).
items.probable_use: Over-worktop socket at the west end of the kitchen run.

items.note: Grey chased conduit ~0.02 m wide running from the floor up to the underside of K9, image (950,900) to (1063,495). Entry at the floor is about 0.15 m west of the socket. Recorded at the midpoint of the run.
items.probable_use: Supply to K9, fed out of the floor screed.

items.note: Loose black cable emerging from a hole in the wall at image (816,404) and hanging free, wobbling down to image (806,610) and on toward the floor line - a free tail roughly 0.9-1.0 m long with no box and no faceplate. 0.63 m west of the east wall corner. x +/-0.20, y +/-0.15 for the exit point.
items.probable_use: Unterminated feed, at hood/worktop height near the hob position - most likely the cooker hood or an appliance circuit left for the fit-out.

items.note: Thin pale line running horizontally WEST away from K9 at about socket height, image (1115,490) to (1230,520). It could be a shallow horizontal chase continuing the circuit along the wall, or just a hairline crack / trowel mark. Recorded at its western visible end; the x given is the furthest point I can see, the run starts at K9. Treat as unconfirmed.
items.probable_use: If real, a horizontal chase carrying the kitchen worktop circuit further west.

items.wall: step wall west face x=+2.15 (faces the living room, z -0.805..-1.405)
items.note: White box at image (47-93, 777-800), i.e. about 0.14 x 0.07 m on the wall - the width says double socket, but at this blur I can only clearly see one dark round recess, so a single socket or an open pattress cannot be excluded. Height taken from the visible floor line at that column (y~884 px), giving 0.29 m; the full back-projection gives 0.14 m, which I believe is wrong because the fitted floor plane there is 0.05 m out. z +/-0.08, y +/-0.10.
items.probable_use: General socket on the 0.60 m return beside the living-room / hall passage.

items.note: Grey chased conduit enters K13 from BELOW (down to the floor, image (75,875)) and a second one leaves it going UP and out of the top of the visible area (image (55,705) and beyond). So this point is a through/loop box, not an end of line, and something else is fed from above - probably a switch or a second socket higher on this return, which is cut off by the frame. Recorded at the midpoint of the upward run; its destination is undocumented.
items.probable_use: Loop to a higher device on the same return.

items.wall: ceiling (slab soffit) near the east wall
items.note: Two features in the bare slab soffit just west of the east wall: a small metal nub at image (535,8) back-projecting to about (x 3.01, z +0.13) and a dark cavity/recess at image (580,32) back-projecting to about (x 3.14, z +0.33). The cavity could be a cable hole left in the slab or simply a formwork blowhole; the nub is probably a cast-in anchor. Recorded as one low-confidence feature at the midpoint. x,z +/-0.25.
items.probable_use: Possibly a ceiling cable outlet for a kitchen light; possibly nothing electrical at all.

items.note: Panel radiator under the window, image x 490-627, y 600-664. Mapped with the west-wall lateral scale of 102.5 px/m (which is fixed by the window frame matching the plan's 1.70 opening): spans z = -1.23 to +0.10, i.e. about 1.33 m long, centred z=-0.57, bottom at y~0.23 and top at y~0.70, so a 500 mm high panel on ~0.23 m legs/brackets. Position given is the centre. z +/-0.10, y +/-0.08. Flow/return pipes not visible (they disappear behind the panel).
items.probable_use: Existing heating emitter - fixed constraint under the living-room window.

items.note: Small bright object image (637-645, 644-655), wedged into the north corner immediately beyond the right-hand end of the radiator and ~0.04 m off the corner. Too small and too blurred to classify: could be a socket, a blank box, or just the radiator's return pipe / wall bracket. Height from the proportional method. z +/-0.06, y +/-0.08.
items.probable_use: Unclear - either a corner socket or heating pipework. Verify on site.

items.note: White plate with one dark recess, image (280-297, 735-750), with a short grey chased conduit running down from it to the floor at image (300,787). Height by the proportional method using the local floor line (y=811.7 px) and ceiling line (y=187.8 px) at that column: 11.2% of 2.70 = 0.30 m, i.e. a textbook low socket. x +/-0.35 (three independent along-wall methods gave -0.70, -0.80 and -0.96 - see the discrepancy note), y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: General living-room socket.

items.note: White plate with one dark recess, image (110-140, 1017-1057), nearest the camera on the south wall, with a grey conduit running down-left from it toward the floor and a thin chase line heading up-right. Proportional height: 10.0% of 2.70 = 0.27 m. x +/-0.45 (methods gave +1.09, +1.48, +1.75), y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: General living-room socket, roughly mid-room on the neighbours' wall.

items.note: White plate image (793-813, 742-762) with a grey conduit running down from it to the floor at image (790,807) and a thin line continuing up-left. Sits at almost the same image row as L3, so it is roughly OPPOSITE L3 across the room. Height 0.235 m by the depth-paired floor-line method. x +/-0.40, y +/-0.08.
items.probable_use: General living-room socket on the bedroom-side wall - the natural TV / sofa wall.

items.note: Black cable emerging from the bare slab at image (565-610, 148-180) and hanging down to a lit temporary bulb at image (595,345). Located by the ceiling-plane ray: ~3.8 m in front of a camera that is ~6.5 m from the west wall, i.e. roughly 0.8 m west of the room centre line and ~0.4 m north of the room's centre in z. x +/-0.5, z +/-0.4.
items.probable_use: Living-room lighting point (currently a builder's lamp).

items.note: Round white ring with a dark centre set into the slab at image (605-623, 113-132), about 0.3 m from L6. A moulded circular ceiling outlet / lamp box. It may well be the same lighting point as L6 with the cable emerging beside it rather than through it. x,z +/-0.4.
items.probable_use: Ceiling light outlet box.

items.note: A thick dark surface-run conduit crosses the bare soffit diagonally from image (585,0) - i.e. from the kitchen/east direction, behind and above the camera - down to about image (563,155) where it terminates at the L6/L7 light point. It runs on the slab surface, not chased. Recorded at the mid-point of the visible length; the run continues east out of frame, so its origin (presumably a switch drop or the board) is undocumented. x,z +/-0.6.
items.probable_use: Lighting circuit feeding the living-room ceiling point from the east.

items.note: Left pad of three groups on the north wall. RED cap at image (305,633) - hot. Two grey conduits run down from this pad to the floor fillet. Mapped with the north wall spanning image x 256-694 at the floor for the plan's 1.23-3.45 (2.22 m), with a trapezoid correction for height. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: Hot feed - most likely the bath/shower mixer or a basin, left high.

items.note: BLUE cap at image (337,635), 0.16 m right of W1 on the same plaster pad. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07. No waste stub anywhere near this pair - the nearest is W5, 0.7 m away.
items.probable_use: Cold feed paired with W1.

items.note: RED cap at image (468,682) on the middle plaster pad. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: Hot feed for the basin or washing machine (paired with W4, drained by W5).

items.note: BLUE cap at image (498,680), 0.15 m right of W3. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: Cold feed paired with W3.

items.note: Grey circular pipe mouth at image (482,705), directly below and between W3/W4, clearly smaller than W7 - reads as a 50 mm socket. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: 50 mm waste for the basin or washing machine served by W3/W4.

items.note: A single BLUE cap at image (632-643, 663-677), no hot partner, with a grey conduit running down from it to the floor. Cold only. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.07.
items.probable_use: Cold supply to the WC cistern (cold-only + a large waste below is the classic toilet rough-in).

items.note: Large grey pipe mouth at image (643-658, 718-735), visibly bigger than W5 and very low - reads as a 110 mm socket. 0.07 m right of W6. x +/-0.08, y +/-0.06.
items.probable_use: 110 mm WC outlet.

items.wall: floor along the north wall z~-4.10
items.note: Exposed grey 110 mm soil pipe laid on the screed along the foot of the north wall, image y 767-813, running from an upturned elbow at the west end (image (368,770), about x=1.80) eastwards past a branch tee near image (487,780) to the east corner at image (717,803). It is NOT buried - it lies in a shallow rebate behind a mortar fillet. Recorded at mid-length, y is the pipe axis. x range 1.8-3.4 +/-0.15.
items.probable_use: Main bathroom drain run collecting W5/W7 and the bath; it sets the minimum floor build-up in the bathroom.

items.wall: bathroom east wall x=+3.45 (within ~0.1 m of the north corner)
items.note: White surface box at image (690-722, 455-485), its face an open dark recess with a pattern of small round holes - that reads as an open pattress/junction box with a terminal block or a cable gland plate, NOT a finished socket. A vertical chased conduit runs from it down the corner to the floor (image column ~694, y 470 to 755). The box straddles the north/east corner line in the image; I read its centre as being on the EAST wall because its face is strongly foreshortened as seen from the doorway, but a position on the north wall right at the corner cannot be excluded. z +/-0.10, y +/-0.12.
items.probable_use: The bathroom's only visible electrical point - plausibly the supply for a washing machine, a water heater, or the feed-in for bathroom lighting/extract.

items.wall: hall north wall z=-2.68 (west of the bathroom door)
items.note: A white plate at image (50-118, 890-935) with a clearly moulded ROCKER - this is a one-gang SWITCH, not a socket (kind 'junction-box' used because the schema has no switch value; treat as switch-box). A thin chase/cable runs horizontally right from it toward the door reveal, and another line runs up-left. Position derived from the off-axis angle against a camera ~0.5 m south of the door plane: ~0.46 m left of the door centre line, so just beside the left reveal (door is x 2.04-2.74). x +/-0.15, y +/-0.20 (the vertical scale at the extreme frame corner is the weakest number in this file).
items.probable_use: Light switch for the bathroom, mounted beside its door.

items.wall: hall north wall z=-2.68 (east of the bathroom door)
items.note: White box at image (815-870, 1200-1240) in the extreme bottom-right corner of the bathroom photo, with a black cable emerging from it and running up-right out of frame (visible to image (860,1125)). Because the cable is loose and the box face is dark/open, I read this as a box with an unterminated tail rather than a finished socket, but the corner of a wide-angle frame is the worst place to judge. Just east of the door's right reveal (x 2.74). x +/-0.15, y +/-0.25.
items.probable_use: Hall socket or the feed-in/loop box for the hall circuit.

items.note: White box with one dark round recess at image (1203-1230, 608-640) in photo-bedroom.png, with a grey conduit running down from it toward the floor (visible to image y~700). Height 0.30 m from the conduit length against the local plate-width scale; that is also the height every other general socket in this flat sits at. The ALONG-WALL x is poor: the photo is a cropped video screenshot so its principal point is unknown, and three estimates spread from -1.2 to -2.7. x +/-0.8, y +/-0.10.
items.probable_use: General bedroom socket on the outer wall - likely a bedside position.

items.note: Panel radiator under the bedroom window, image x 715-955, y 425-490. Mapped with the west-wall scale fixed by the window frame (170 px/m): spans z = -4.17 to -2.76, about 1.41 m long, centred z=-3.46. Its height above the floor is the unreliable part - the floor line at the window is only approximately locatable in this screenshot, so the panel sits somewhere in y 0.15-0.65. Position given is the centre of the panel. z +/-0.12, y +/-0.25.
items.probable_use: Existing heating emitter under the bedroom window.

items.note: A lit temporary bulb hanging on a black cable, image (885-900, 25-70). The cable runs up and OUT of the top of the frame, so the point where it leaves the slab is not in the photo and I cannot locate it. The x,z given is a guess at roughly the middle of the bedroom, biased toward the window/north where the bulb appears. x +/-1.0, z +/-0.8.
items.probable_use: Bedroom lighting point (currently a builder's lamp).

items.note: A small pale patch with a dark streak below it at image (395-412, 935-990) on the near (living-room-side) wall of the bedroom. At this resolution I cannot distinguish a socket plus conduit from a scuff mark plus shadow; I record it only because its shape and position match the socket+conduit pattern seen everywhere else. x +/-0.8, y +/-0.2.
items.probable_use: If real, a general bedroom socket on the inner wall.

items.note: A dark blob roughly 0.05-0.08 m across at image (460-472, 630-655), essentially at the floor line, about 0.5 m from the window-wall corner. Could be a floor-level box or hole, could be a chipped patch of plaster or a shadow. Honest answer: indeterminate, listed so it is not lost. x +/-0.6, y +/-0.10.
items.probable_use: Unknown.
